======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioner/s : Mr. Dr. Mayanand Jha
 For the Respondent/s : None
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Kishore Kumar
 Mandal
 Oral Order
2 19-07-2016
Heard Dr. Jha for the petitioner.
No one has appeared on behalf of the State.
Petitioner runs a vending sweets shop.
For adulterating the sweets he was proceeded against under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 ( for short 'the Act').
The report of the analysis at the laboratory was furnished to the petitioner.

After affording opportunity of hearing to both sides , the authority under the Act passed the order dated 30.10.2013 imposing fine of Rs.
25,000/- (Twenty Five thousand) (Annexure-6) which is impugned in the writ application.
In para- 18 it is stated that Food Safety Appellate Tribunal is not functioning .
Mr. Jha has fairly stated that the Tribunal constituted under Section 76 of the Act is now functioning.
Any appeal could have been filed before the appellate authority /Tribunal within 45 days.
Seen thus, the petitioner has statutory remedy available to assail the order where all questions of fact and law can be agitated.

Declining the relief, as prayed in the application, the Court grants the petitioner liberty to file appeal against the aforesaid order dated 30.10.2013 before the appellate authority after seeking condonation of delay, if any, on the ground that the petitioner had been Deep Shankar vs The State Of Bihar & Ors on 19 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126181120/
1 bonafidely pursuing his remedy before this Court.
